[0] A California Apple user has filed a class action lawsuit accusing Apple of misleading consumers about its privacy-focused "Hide My Email" feature. Here are the details.

[1] Apple accused of hiding vulnerabilities in its “Hide My Email” feature

[2] A few days ago, 404 Media reported that Apple has been aware of a vulnerability for over a year that could expose the real email addresses behind aliases generated by "Hide My Email".

[3] Apple's "Hide My Email" feature lets users create unique, randomly generated email addresses that forward messages to a user's personal inbox, so they can sign up for apps, websites, or newsletters without revealing their true email addresses.

[4] The feature is available for free through "Sign in with Apple", while iCloud+ plans (starting at US$0.99 per month) include a more robust version that lets users create aliases for websites, newsletters and other services.

[5] According to 404 Media, a security researcher alerted Apple in June 2025 about a vulnerability that could leak the real email addresses behind "Hide My Email" aliases.

[6] Apple acknowledged receiving the report about a month later, but allegedly took no action to fix the issue. Apple claimed it had fixed the flaw in March 2026, but the researcher found it could still be exploited.

[7] Excerpt from 404 Media:

[8] Regarding the lawsuit (reported by MacRumors), plaintiff Anthony Alvarez says:

[9] Apple knew about the issue over a year ago, but the vulnerability remains unfixed — meanwhile, Apple continues to profit from "Hide My Email" and its privacy promises. The plaintiff is one of millions of paying iCloud+ subscribers who relied on Apple's statements that "Hide My Email" would protect his personal email address. Plaintiffs and class members paid Apple for privacy — iCloud+ subscribers through the premium baked into their subscription fees, and all Apple customers through what Apple products include, which Apple markets as offering

[10] The lawsuit also argues this is not an isolated incident, citing a 2023 report that Apple's randomized MAC address feature may leak users' actual hardware identifiers.

[11] The complaint also alleges that the proposed class members' claims total more than US$5 million (excluding interest and attorneys' fees), but doesn't explain how it arrived at that figure.

[12] Alvarez filed suit on behalf of himself and other Apple customers he claims were affected. He wants the court to certify the case as a class action covering four proposed groups of users:

  • [13] A nationwide Apple customer class whose members have purchased devices and used "Hide My Email";
  • [14] A California subclass of those users;
  • [15] A nationwide subclass of iCloud+ subscribers who have used the feature;
  • [16] A California subclass of iCloud+ subscribers.

[17] He wants a jury trial and is seeking, in addition to unspecified monetary damages, a court order requiring Apple to either fix "Hide My Email" or clearly disclose its limitations.

[18] Apple has not yet responded to the lawsuit.
